source.benchmark: One Night Ultimate Werewolf, the paper's adversarial setting (ONUW environment of Jin et al., NeurIPS 2024)
source.setup: 5 players, roles fixed across games as in the paper's runs: player1 Troublemaker, player2 Werewolf, player3 Seer, player4 Robber, player5 Villager; center cards Werewolf, Villager, Insomniac. 3 discussion rounds, then one vote.
source.plugin: All five players use EvolveMAS (online memory and cross-game knowledge).
differences_from_original: The Seer's center check shows 2 of the 3 real center cards (the original samples from the full candidate list).
All final roles are revealed after the vote so partner profiles can learn from ground truth; the original reveals only the voted player's role.
If no player holds a Werewolf card, Village wins only if no one dies (the original calls this a draw).
source.not_the_paper_run: Recorded for this demo with the open-source plug-in; not the experiment run behind the paper's tables.

[to player1 only] Your role card is Troublemaker.
[to player2 only] Your role card is Werewolf.
[to player3 only] Your role card is Seer.
[to player4 only] Your role card is Robber.

events.prompt:
You are playing One Night Ultimate Werewolf with 4 other players (player1 to player5).

Roles: there are 8 candidate roles: 2 Villagers, 2 Werewolves, 1 Seer, 1 Robber, 1 Troublemaker, 1 Insomniac.
Each player got one role; the other 3 are face down in the center, so some roles may not be in play.
- Villager: no ability.
- Werewolf (Team Werewolf): at night, sees the other Werewolves among the players.
- Seer: at night, looks at one other player's role, or at two of the center cards.
- Robber: at night, may swap their card with another player's card and then sees their new role.
- Troublemaker: at night, may swap the cards of two other players without looking at them.
- Insomniac: at the end of the night, sees their own final card.
Everyone except Werewolves is on Team Village. Night order: Werewolf, Seer, Robber, Troublemaker, Insomniac.
Because cards can be swapped at night, your final role may differ from the role you started with,
and your team is decided by your FINAL card.

Day: 3 rounds of open discussion. You may say anything, including lying about your role; you cannot show your card.
Vote: everyone votes for one other player. The player with the most votes dies.
Team Village wins if at least one Werewolf dies (or if no player is a Werewolf and no one dies).
Team Werewolf wins if at least one player is a Werewolf and no Werewolf dies.
If the top vote count is only 1, no one dies.

You are player3. Your starting role is Seer.

What you have seen and heard so far in this game:
moderator: Night falls. Everyone, close your eyes.
moderator: Your role card is Seer.

NIGHT ACTION (Seer). Choose: {"check": "<playerN>"} to look at one other player's role, or {"check": "center"} to look at two center cards. Add "thought": "<why>".
Answer with one JSON object only.
events.reply: {"check": "player1", "thought": "I want to see if player1 is a Werewolf to confirm the team composition early."}

events.content: [to player3 only] You looked at player1's card: Troublemaker.

You are playing One Night Ultimate Werewolf with 4 other players (player1 to player5).

Roles: there are 8 candidate roles: 2 Villagers, 2 Werewolves, 1 Seer, 1 Robber, 1 Troublemaker, 1 Insomniac.
Each player got one role; the other 3 are face down in the center, so some roles may not be in play.
- Villager: no ability.
- Werewolf (Team Werewolf): at night, sees the other Werewolves among the players.
- Seer: at night, looks at one other player's role, or at two of the center cards.
- Robber: at night, may swap their card with another player's card and then sees their new role.
- Troublemaker: at night, may swap the cards of two other players without looking at them.
- Insomniac: at the end of the night, sees their own final card.
Everyone except Werewolves is on Team Village. Night order: Werewolf, Seer, Robber, Troublemaker, Insomniac.
Because cards can be swapped at night, your final role may differ from the role you started with,
and your team is decided by your FINAL card.

Day: 3 rounds of open discussion. You may say anything, including lying about your role; you cannot show your card.
Vote: everyone votes for one other player. The player with the most votes dies.
Team Village wins if at least one Werewolf dies (or if no player is a Werewolf and no one dies).
Team Werewolf wins if at least one player is a Werewolf and no Werewolf dies.
If the top vote count is only 1, no one dies.

events.prompt:
You are playing One Night Ultimate Werewolf with 4 other players (player1 to player5).

Roles: there are 8 candidate roles: 2 Villagers, 2 Werewolves, 1 Seer, 1 Robber, 1 Troublemaker, 1 Insomniac.
Each player got one role; the other 3 are face down in the center, so some roles may not be in play.
- Villager: no ability.
- Werewolf (Team Werewolf): at night, sees the other Werewolves among the players.
- Seer: at night, looks at one other player's role, or at two of the center cards.
- Robber: at night, may swap their card with another player's card and then sees their new role.
- Troublemaker: at night, may swap the cards of two other players without looking at them.
- Insomniac: at the end of the night, sees their own final card.
Everyone except Werewolves is on Team Village. Night order: Werewolf, Seer, Robber, Troublemaker, Insomniac.
Because cards can be swapped at night, your final role may differ from the role you started with,
and your team is decided by your FINAL card.

Day: 3 rounds of open discussion. You may say anything, including lying about your role; you cannot show your card.
Vote: everyone votes for one other player. The player with the most votes dies.
Team Village wins if at least one Werewolf dies (or if no player is a Werewolf and no one dies).
Team Werewolf wins if at least one player is a Werewolf and no Werewolf dies.
If the top vote count is only 1, no one dies.

You are player5. Your starting role is Villager.

What you have seen and heard so far in this game:
moderator: Night falls. Everyone, close your eyes.
moderator: Your role card is Villager.
moderator: Day breaks. Everyone, open your eyes. Discussion begins with player1.
player1: I swapped the cards of player2 and player4 last night, so their roles changed. Player2 is now the Werewolf, and player4 ended up as the Robber. We need to focus on rooting out the real Werewolf before the vote.
player2: I didn’t swap with anyone last night, so player1’s story doesn’t add up—if they say player4 is the Robber, then either they’re lying or confused. Let’s be careful before we jump to conclusions about who the Werewolf really is.
player3: I’m the Seer and I looked at two center cards last night—there’s definitely an Insomniac and a Werewolf there, so neither of those roles started with a player. Player1’s story about swapping Player2 and Player4 makes sense given what I saw; Player2 is the Werewolf now, and Player4 is the Robber. We should focus on Player2 as the main threat.
player4: I was the Robber and swapped with player2, so I’m now the Werewolf. Player1 says they swapped player2 and me, but that would mean I’m still Robber, which I’m not. Let's focus on the facts: player2 is now the Robber and player4 is the Werewolf. We need to target player4 to protect the Village.
player5: Player3’s Seer claim matches player1’s story, so I trust that player2 is the Werewolf now. We should focus on voting out player2 to keep the Village safe.
player1: Let's stay focused on the facts: Player2 ended up as the Werewolf after my swap, and Player4 is the Robber now. Player4’s claim trying to flip the roles doesn't match what I did. We need to vote out Player2 to keep the Village safe.
player2: I’m telling you, I never swapped roles last night—I started and ended as the Werewolf. Player4’s story doesn’t add up; if they really swapped with me, they would be the Werewolf now, not the Robber. Let’s focus on the facts and not get distracted.
player3: Given what I saw in the center and the swaps Player1 described, Player2 is definitely the Werewolf now, and Player4 is the Robber. Player4’s claim doesn’t fit with the facts, so we should focus on voting out Player2 to protect the Village.
player4: I swapped with player2 and became the Werewolf, so player2 is now the Robber. Player1’s claim about swapping us doesn’t fit with what I actually did. Let’s focus on voting out player2 to keep the Village safe.

Roles: there are 8 candidate roles: 2 Villagers, 2 Werewolves, 1 Seer, 1 Robber, 1 Troublemaker, 1 Insomniac.
Each player got one role; the other 3 are face down in the center, so some roles may not be in play.
- Villager: no ability.
- Werewolf (Team Werewolf): at night, sees the other Werewolves among the players.
- Seer: at night, looks at one other player's role, or at two of the center cards.
- Robber: at night, may swap their card with another player's card and then sees their new role.
- Troublemaker: at night, may swap the cards of two other players without looking at them.
- Insomniac: at the end of the night, sees their own final card.
Everyone except Werewolves is on Team Village. Night order: Werewolf, Seer, Robber, Troublemaker, Insomniac.
Because cards can be swapped at night, your final role may differ from the role you started with,
and your team is decided by your FINAL card.

Day: 3 rounds of open discussion. You may say anything, including lying about your role; you cannot show your card.
Vote: everyone votes for one other player. The player with the most votes dies.
Team Village wins if at least one Werewolf dies (or if no player is a Werewolf and no one dies).
Team Werewolf wins if at least one player is a Werewolf and no Werewolf dies.
If the top vote count is only 1, no one dies.

You are player1. Your starting role is Troublemaker.

What you have seen and heard so far in this game:
moderator: Night falls. Everyone, close your eyes.
moderator: Your role card is Troublemaker.
moderator: You swapped the cards of player2 and player4.
moderator: Day breaks. Everyone, open your eyes. Discussion begins with player1.
player1: I’m the Troublemaker and swapped player2 and player4’s roles last night. So whatever roles they’re claiming now might be switched—keep that in mind when you decide who to trust. Let’s figure out who’s really a Werewolf before voting.
player2: I’m not the Werewolf anymore—player1’s Troublemaker claim means I could be something else now. Let’s focus on who actually switched roles and figure out who’s still dangerous before pointing fingers.
player3: I’m the Seer and I looked at the center cards last night—there’s a Villager and an Insomniac there, so those roles aren’t in play with us. That means the roles among players are likely Villager, Werewolf, Troublemaker, Robber, and maybe one more. Let’s focus on who might be Werewolf now.
player4: I’m the Robber and swapped with player2, who I now know is a Werewolf. Player1 claims to be the Troublemaker who swapped player2 and me, which matches what I did, so I trust their claim. Player3’s Seer info checks out too—let’s focus on finding the other Werewolf.
player5: I trust player3’s Seer claim, and player4’s confession about swapping with player2 who is Werewolf makes sense. Player1’s Troublemaker role checks out too. Player2 seems like the obvious Werewolf to vote for—any thoughts?

[Your memory]
Working memory for this episode:
Player1 has confirmed their Troublemaker role and the swaps. Player2 denies being the Werewolf. Player4 supports player1's claim. Next, they need to identify the Werewolf.

- player2_role_reveal: Player2's role is now unknown after the swap with player4, but they claim not to be the Werewolf anymore. (medium)

Known facts:
- troublemaker_role: Player1's role is Troublemaker. (high)

- player1_role: Player1's role is Troublemaker. (high)

Interaction Strategies (learned from earlier episodes):
- If you are the Troublemaker, claim to have swapped roles with two players to create confusion.
- When another player claims to have swapped roles, verify their claim by observing their behavior and statements.
- If a player expresses confusion about their role after a swap, consider them a potential threat and discuss their vote carefully.
- Encourage voting against players who claim to be Werewolves, especially if their claims are inconsistent with other players' information.
- Support players who provide accurate information and align with the Village's interests.

Partner Profiles:
- player2: Expresses confusion about their role and seeks clarification after a swap. (reliability: low - their role was the Werewolf, which they did not initially acknowledge.)
- player3: Provides accurate information and warns against trusting claims without verification. (reliability: high - consistently supported truthful claims.)
- player4: Claims to be a Werewolf after a swap, which may be misleading. (reliability: low - ultimately revealed to be the Robber and misled others.)
- player5: Supports claims made by others and focuses on protecting the Village. (reliability: high - consistently aligned with the Village's interests.)

DISCUSSION round 2 of 3. Speak to the table in 1-3 sentences, in character as a player trying to win for your team. Output only what you say.

You are playing One Night Ultimate Werewolf with 4 other players (player1 to player5).

Roles: there are 8 candidate roles: 2 Villagers, 2 Werewolves, 1 Seer, 1 Robber, 1 Troublemaker, 1 Insomniac.
Each player got one role; the other 3 are face down in the center, so some roles may not be in play.
- Villager: no ability.
- Werewolf (Team Werewolf): at night, sees the other Werewolves among the players.
- Seer: at night, looks at one other player's role, or at two of the center cards.
- Robber: at night, may swap their card with another player's card and then sees their new role.
- Troublemaker: at night, may swap the cards of two other players without looking at them.
- Insomniac: at the end of the night, sees their own final card.
Everyone except Werewolves is on Team Village. Night order: Werewolf, Seer, Robber, Troublemaker, Insomniac.
Because cards can be swapped at night, your final role may differ from the role you started with,
and your team is decided by your FINAL card.

Day: 3 rounds of open discussion. You may say anything, including lying about your role; you cannot show your card.
Vote: everyone votes for one other player. The player with the most votes dies.
Team Village wins if at least one Werewolf dies (or if no player is a Werewolf and no one dies).
Team Werewolf wins if at least one player is a Werewolf and no Werewolf dies.
If the top vote count is only 1, no one dies.
